Main.sentence: Israeli settlements , also called Israeli colonies ,     are the civilian communities built by ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ throughout the ___E:Israeli-occupied territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ .

They are populated by Israeli citizens, almost exclusively of ___E:Jewish identity or ethnicity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Jews)___ ,    and have been constructed on lands that Israel has militarily occupied since the ___E:Six-Day War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ in 1967.  The international community considers ___E:Israeli settlements to be illegal under international law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law_and_Israeli_settlements)___ ,     but Israel disputes this.     In 2024, the ___E:International Court of Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice)___ (ICJ) found in an advisory opinion that Israel's occupation was illegal and ruled that Israel had "an obligation to cease immediately all new settlement activities and to evacuate all settlers" from the occupied territories.
The expansion of settlements often involves the confiscation of Palestinian land and resources, leading to displacement of Palestinian communities and creating a source of tension and conflict.
Settlements are often protected by the Israeli military and are frequently flashpoints for violence against Palestinians.

Furthermore, the presence of settlements and Jewish-only bypass roads creates a ___E:fragmented Palestinian territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories)___ , seriously hindering economic development and ___E:freedom of movement for Palestinians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_freedom_of_movement)___ .

As of April 2025, Israeli settlements exist in the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank#Settlement)___ (including ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ ), which is claimed by the ___E:Palestine Liberation Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization)___ (PLO) as the sovereign territory of the ___E:State of Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Palestine)___ , and in the ___E:Golan Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights#Israeli_settlements)___ , which is internationally recognized as a part of the sovereign territory of ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ . [a] Through the ___E:Jerusalem Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem_Law)___ and the ___E:Golan Heights Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights_Law)___ , Israel effectively annexed both territories, though the international community has rejected any change to their ___E:status as occupied territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_territories_occupied_by_Israel_in_1967)___ .

Although Israel's West Bank settlements have been built on territory administered under military rule rather than civil law, ___E:Israeli civil law is "pipelined" into the settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_law_in_the_West_Bank_settlements)___ , such that Israeli citizens living there are treated similarly to those living in Israel.
Many consider it to be a major obstacle to the ___E:Israeli–Palestinian peace process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_process)___ .

In Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (2004), the ICJ found that Israel's settlements and the then-nascent ___E:Israeli West Bank barrier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_West_Bank_barrier)___ were both in violation of international law; part of the latter has been constructed within the West Bank, as opposed to being entirely on Israel's side of the ___E:Green Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel))___ .

As of January 2023, [needs update] there are ___E:144 Israeli settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Israeli_settlements)___ in the West Bank, including 12 in East Jerusalem; the Israeli government administers the West Bank as the ___E:Judea and Samaria Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judea_and_Samaria_Area)___ , which does not include East Jerusalem.

In addition to the settlements, the West Bank is also hosting at least 196 ___E:Israeli outposts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_outpost)___ ,  which are settlements that have not been authorized by the Israeli government.
In total, over 450,000 Israeli settlers reside in the West Bank, excluding East Jerusalem, with an additional 220,000 Israeli settlers residing in East Jerusalem.
Additionally, over 25,000 Israeli settlers live in Syria's Golan Heights.

Between 1967 and 1982, there were 18 settlements established in the ___E:Israeli-occupied Sinai Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_Sinai_Peninsula)___ of ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ , though these were dismantled by Israel after the ___E:Egypt–Israel peace treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty)___ of 1979. Additionally, as part of the ___E:Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_disengagement_from_Gaza)___ in 2005, Israel dismantled all 21 settlements in the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ and four settlements in the West Bank.

Per the ___E:Fourth Geneva Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Geneva_Convention)___ , the transfer by an occupying power of its civilian population into the territory it is occupying constitutes a ___E:war crime U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crime)___ ,    although Israel disputes that this statute applies to the West Bank.   On 20 December 2019, the ___E:International Criminal Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court)___ announced the opening of ___E:an investigation of war crimes in the Palestinian territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court_investigation_in_Palestine)___ .

The presence and ongoing expansion of existing settlements by Israel and the construction of outposts is frequently criticized as an obstacle to peace by the PLO,  and by a number of third parties, such as the ___E:Organization of Islamic Cooperation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation)___ ,  the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ (UN),  Russia,   the United Kingdom,  France,  and the ___E:European Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ .
The UN has repeatedly upheld the view that Israel's construction of settlements in the occupied territories constitutes a violation of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

For decades, the United States also designated Israeli settlements as illegal,  but the ___E:first Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Trump_administration)___ reversed this long-standing policy in November 2019,  declaring that "the establishment of Israeli civilian settlements in the West Bank is not per se inconsistent with international law";  this new policy, in turn, was reversed to the original by the ___E:Biden administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden)___ in February 2024, once again classifying Israeli settlement expansion as "inconsistent with international law" and matching the official positions of the other three members of the ___E:Middle East Quartet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartet_on_the_Middle_East)___ .   [needs update?]
Certain observers and Palestinians occasionally use the term "Israeli colonies" as a substitute for the term "settlements".
Settlements range in character from farming communities and frontier villages to urban suburbs and neighborhoods.

The four largest settlements, ___E:Modi'in Illit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modi%27in_Illit)___ , ___E:Ma'ale Adumim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%27ale_Adumim)___ , ___E:Beitar Illit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beitar_Illit)___ and ___E:Ariel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_(city))___ , have achieved city status.
Ariel has 18,000 residents, while the rest have around 37,000 to 55,500 each.

Settlement has an economic dimension, much of it driven by the significantly lower costs of housing for Israeli citizens living in Israeli settlements compared to the cost of housing and living in Israel proper.

Government spending per citizen in the settlements is double that spent per Israeli citizen in ___E:Tel Aviv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv)___ and ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ , while government spending for settlers in isolated Israeli settlements is three times the Israeli national average.
Most of the spending goes to the security of the Israeli citizens living there.

As of January 2023, there are 144 Israeli settlements in the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ , including 12 in ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ .

In addition, there are at least 196 ___E:Israeli illegal outposts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_outpost)___ (not sanctioned by the Israeli government) in the West Bank.  In total, over 500,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank excluding East Jerusalem,   with an additional 220,000 Jewish settlers residing in East Jerusalem.
Additionally, over 20,000 Israeli citizens live in settlements in the Golan Heights.
Following the 1967 ___E:Six-Day War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ , Israel ___E:occupied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_occupation)___ a number of territories.

It took over the remainder of the Palestinian Mandate territories of the ___E:West Bank including East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank)___ , from ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ which had ___E:controlled the territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank)___ since the 1948 Arab-Israeli war, and the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ from ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ , which had ___E:held Gaza under occupation since 1949 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_Egypt)___ .

From Egypt, it also captured the ___E:Sinai Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula)___ and from ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ it captured most of the ___E:Golan Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights)___ , which ___E:since 1981 has been administered under the Golan Heights Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_the_Golan_Heights)___ .

As early as September 1967, Israeli settlement policy was progressively encouraged by the ___E:Labor government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_government_of_Israel)___ of ___E:Levi Eshkol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Eshkol)___ .

The basis for Israeli settlement in the West Bank became the ___E:Allon Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allon_Plan)___ ,   named after its inventor ___E:Yigal Allon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yigal_Allon)___ .

It implied Israeli annexation of major parts of the ___E:Israeli-occupied territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ , especially ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ , ___E:Gush Etzion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Etzion)___ and the ___E:Jordan Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Valley_(Middle_East))___ .
The settlement policy of the government of Yitzhak Rabin was also derived from the Allon Plan.

The first settlement was ___E:Kfar Etzion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kfar_Etzion)___ , in the southern West Bank,   although that location was outside the Allon Plan. Many settlements began as ___E:Nahal settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahal_settlement)___ .
They were established as military outposts and later expanded and populated with civilian inhabitants.

According to a secret document dating to 1970, obtained by ___E:Haaretz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haaretz)___ , the settlement of ___E:Kiryat Arba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiryat_Arba)___ was established by confiscating land by military order and falsely representing the project as being strictly for military use while in reality, Kiryat Arba was planned for settler use. The method of confiscating land by military order for establishing civilian settlements was an open secret in Israel throughout the 1970s, but publication of the information was suppressed by the ___E:military censor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Military_Censor)___ .
In the 1970s, Israel's methods for seizing Palestinian land to establish settlements included requisitioning for ostensibly military purposes and spraying of land with poison.

The Likud government of Menahem Begin, from 1977, was more supportive to settlement in other parts of the West Bank, by organizations like ___E:Gush Emunim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Emunim)___ and the ___E:Jewish Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Agency_for_Israel)___ /World Zionist Organization, and intensified the settlement activities.

In a government statement, Likud declared that the entire historic Land of Israel is the inalienable heritage of the Jewish people and that no part of the West Bank should be handed over to foreign rule.  Ariel Sharon declared in the same year (1977) that there was a plan to settle 2 million Jews in the West Bank by 2000.  The government abrogated the prohibition from purchasing occupied land by Israelis; the "Drobles Plan", a plan for large-scale settlement in the West Bank meant to prevent a Palestinian state under the pretext of security became the framework for its policy.  [A] The "Drobles Plan" from the ___E:World Zionist Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Zionist_Organization)___ , dated October 1978 and named "Master Plan for the Development of Settlements in Judea and Samaria, 1979–1983", was written by the Jewish Agency director and former Knesset member ___E:Matityahu Drobles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matityahu_Drobles)___ .

In January 1981, the government adopted a follow-up plan from Drobles, dated September 1980 and named "The current state of the settlements in Judea and Samaria", with more details about settlement strategy and policy.  [B]

Since 1967, government-funded settlement projects in the West Bank are implemented by the "Settlement Division" of the ___E:World Zionist Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Zionist_Organization)___ .

Though formally a ___E:non-governmental organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-governmental_organization)___ , it is funded by the Israeli government and leases lands from the Civil Administration to settle in the West Bank. It is authorized to create settlements in the West Bank on lands licensed to it by the Civil Administration.
Traditionally, the Settlement Division has been under the responsibility of the Agriculture Ministry.
Since the Oslo Accords, it was always housed within the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
In 2007, it was moved back to the Agriculture Ministry.
In 2009, the Netanyahu Government decided to subject all settlement activities to additional approval of the Prime Minister and the Defense Minister.
In 2011, Netanyahu sought to move the Settlement Division again under the direct control of (his own) PMO, and to curtail Defense Minister Ehud Barak's authority.

At the presentation of the ___E:Oslo II Accord U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_II_Accord)___ on 5 October 1995 in the Knesset, PM ___E:Yitzhak Rabin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin)___ expounded the Israeli settlement policy in connection with the permanent solution to the conflict.
Israel wanted "a Palestinian entity, less than a state, which will be a home to most of the Palestinian residents living in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank" .
It wanted to keep settlements beyond the ___E:Green Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel))___ including Ma'ale Adumim and Givat Ze'ev in East Jerusalem.
Blocs of settlements should be established in the West Bank. Rabin promised not to return to the 4 June 1967 lines.
In June 1997, the Likud government of ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ presented its "Allon Plus Plan".

This plan holds the retention of some 60% of the West Bank, including the "Greater Jerusalem" area with the settlements Gush Etzion and Ma'aleh Adumim, other large concentrations of settlements in the West Bank, the entire Jordan Valley, a "security area", and a network of Israeli-only bypass roads.
In the ___E:Road map for peace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_map_for_peace)___ of 2002, which was never implemented, the establishment of a Palestinian state was acknowledged.
Outposts would be dismantled.
However, many new outposts appeared instead, few were removed.
Israel's settlement policy remained unchanged.
Settlements in East Jerusalem and remaining West Bank were expanded.

While according to official Israeli policy no new settlements were built, at least some hundred ___E:unauthorized outposts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_outpost)___ were established since 2002 with ___E:state funding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sasson_Report)___ in the 60% of the West Bank that was not under ___E:Palestinian administrative control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Authority)___ and the population growth of settlers did not diminish.

In 2005, all 21 settlements in the Gaza Strip and four in the northern West Bank were forcibly evacuated as part of ___E:Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_disengagement_from_the_Gaza_Strip)___ , known to some in Israel as "the Expulsion".
Nevertheless, the total settler population continued to rise.

After the failure of the Roadmap, several new plans emerged to settle in major parts of the West Bank. In 2011, Haaretz revealed the ___E:Civil Administration's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Civil_Administration)___ "Blue Line" -plan, written in January 2011, which aims to increase Israeli "state-ownership" of ___E:West Bank land U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declarations_of_State_Land_in_the_West_Bank)___ ("state lands") and settlement in strategic areas like the Jordan Valley and the northern Dead Sea area.  In March 2012, it was revealed that the Civil Administration over the years covertly allotted 10% of the West Bank for further settlement.
Provisional names for future new settlements or settlement expansions were already assigned.
The plan includes many Palestinian built-up sites in the ___E:Areas A and B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_the_Oslo_Accords)___ .
Land in the Gaza Strip available to its Palestinian inhabitants has historically been limited as a result of Israeli land confiscation and the establishment of settlements.

Settlement growth in the Gaza Strip before 1977 was limited, as the Israeli labor party's policy of containment preferred the establishment of a collection of settlements along the border of the Strip.
At this point, 6 settlements in the Strip existed, Kfar Darom, Netzarim, Morag, Eretz, Katif, and Netzer Hazani.

With the Likud party's revisionist Zionist policies entering with Begin's government, the scale of settlement expansion increased, although the basic policies relating to the settlements did not change.
By 1978, 13 settlements had been built as part of a buffer zone along Gaza's southern border in Rafah.

The discussions at ___E:Camp David U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David_Accords)___ that year surrounding the idea of potential future Palestinian autonomy would trigger an increase in settlement expansion in the Gaza Strip, following the Israeli policy of establishing " ___E:facts on the ground U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facts_on_the_ground)___ ".
Political economist Sara Roy described this as a policy intended to make the establishment of an independent Palestinian state more difficult.
The locations and size of these new settlements would contribute to geographically isolating Palestinian communities from each other.
In the seven years between 1978 and 1985, 11,500 acres of land were confiscated by the Israeli government for the establishment of settlements.
By 1991, the settler population in Gaza would reach 3,500 and 4,000 by 1993, or less than 1% of Gaza's population.
The land available for use by the Jewish settler community exceeded 25% of the total land in Gaza. The ratio of dunams to people was 23 for Jewish settlers, and 0.27 for Palestinians.
Comparing the available built-up area available to each of the two groups in 1993, the ratio is 115 people per square mile for Jewish settlers and over 9,000 people per square mile for Palestinians.
Sara Roy estimates the increase in Palestinian population density in Gaza due to Israeli policies alone to be an increase of almost 2,000 people per square mile in 1993.
All the settlements were surrounded by electric fences or barbed wire.

While the settlements maintained an isolated economic system, they affected the Gazan economy via land confiscation, the disproportionate consumption of local resources such as water, by overwhelmingly denying work opportunities and through the large disparities in funding (both private and governmental) for economic development.
Some settlements are self-contained cities with a stable population in the tens of thousands, infrastructure, and all other features of permanence.

Examples are ___E:Beitar Illit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beitar_Illit)___ (a city of close to 45,000 residents), ___E:Ma'ale Adumim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%27ale_Adumim)___ , ___E:Modi'in Illit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modi%27in_Illit)___ , and ___E:Ariel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_(city))___ (almost 20,000 residents).

Some are towns with a ___E:local council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_council_(Israel))___ status with populations of 2,000–20,0000, such as ___E:Alfei Menashe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfei_Menashe)___ , ___E:Eli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli,_Mateh_Binyamin)___ , ___E:Elkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elkana)___ , ___E:Efrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efrat_(Israeli_settlement))___ and ___E:Kiryat Arba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiryat_Arba)___ .

There are also clusters of villages governed by a local elected committee and ___E:regional councils U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_council_(Israel))___ that are responsible for municipal services.

Examples are ___E:Kfar Adumim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kfar_Adumim)___ , ___E:Neve Daniel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neve_Daniel)___ , ___E:Kfar Tapuach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kfar_Tapuach)___ and ___E:Ateret U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateret)___ . ___E:Kibbutzim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibbutz)___ and ___E:moshavim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshav)___ in the territories include ___E:Argaman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argaman)___ , ___E:Gilgal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilgal,_Bik%27at_HaYarden)___ , ___E:Na'aran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Na%27aran_(Israeli_settlement))___ and ___E:Yitav U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitav)___ .
Jewish neighborhoods have been built on the outskirts of Arab neighborhoods, for example in ___E:Hebron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebron)___ .

In Jerusalem, there are urban neighborhoods where Jews and Arabs live together: the ___E:Muslim Quarter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Quarter_(Jerusalem))___ , ___E:Silwan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silwan)___ , ___E:Abu Tor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Tor)___ , ___E:Sheikh Jarrah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Jarrah)___ and ___E:Shimon HaTzadik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_HaTzadik)___ .

Under the ___E:Oslo Accords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords)___ , the West Bank was divided into three separate parts designated as ___E:Area A, Area B and Area C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_the_Oslo_Accords)___ .
Leaving aside the position of East Jerusalem, all of the settlements are in ___E:Area C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_C_(West_Bank))___ which comprises about 60% of the West Bank.

Some settlements were established on sites where Jewish communities had existed during the ___E:British Mandate of Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ or even since the ___E:First Aliyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Aliyah)___ or ancient times.

At the end of 2010, 534,224 Jewish Israelis lived in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. 314,132 of them lived in the 121 authorised settlements and 102 unauthorised settlement outposts on the West Bank, 198,629 were living in East Jerusalem, and almost 20,000 lived in settlements in the Golan Heights.
By 2011, the number of Jewish settlers in the West Bank excluding East Jerusalem had increased to 328,423 people.
In June 2014, the number of Israeli settlers in the West Bank excluding East Jerusalem had increased to 382,031 people, with over 20,000 Israeli settlers in the Golan Heights.
In January 2015, the Israeli Interior Ministry gave figures of 389,250 Israeli citizens living in the West Bank outside East Jerusalem.
By the end of 2016, the West Bank Jewish population had risen to 420,899, excluding East Jerusalem, where there were more than 200,000 Jews.
In 2019, the number of Israeli settlers in the West Bank excluding East Jerusalem had risen to 441,600 individuals,  and the number of Israeli settlers in the Golan Heights had risen to 25,261.
In 2020, the number of Israeli settlers in the West Bank excluding East Jerusalem had reportedly risen to 451,700 individuals, with an additional 220,000 Jews living in East Jerusalem.

In addition to internal migration, in large though declining numbers, the settlements absorb annually about 1000 new immigrants from outside Israel.

The American Kulanu organization works with such right-wing Israeli settler groups as ___E:Amishav and Shavei Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shavei_Israel)___ to settle "lost" Jews of color in such areas where local Palestinians are being displaced.
In the 1990s, the annual settler population growth was more than three times the annual population growth in Israel.
Population growth has continued in the 2000s.

According to the BBC, the settlements in the West Bank have been growing at a rate of 5–6% since 2001.  In 2016, there were sixty thousand ___E:American Israelis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_diaspora)___ living in settlements in the West Bank.

The establishment of settlements in the Palestinian territories is linked to the displacement of the Palestinian populations as evidenced by a 1979 Security Council Commission which established a link between Israeli settlements and the displacement of the local population.

The commission also found that those who remained were under consistent pressure to leave to make room for further settlers who were being encouraged into the area. In conclusion the commission stated that settlement in the Palestinian territories was causing "profound and irreversible changes of a geographic and demographic nature".
The Israeli settlements in the West Bank fall under the administrative district of Judea and Samaria Area .
Since December 2007, approval by both the Israeli Prime Minister and Israeli Defense Minister of all settlement activities (including planning) in the West Bank is required.

Authority for planning and construction is held by the ___E:Israel Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces)___ ___E:Civil Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Civil_Administration)___ .

The area consists of four ___E:cities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_council_(Israel))___ , thirteen ___E:local councils U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_council_(Israel))___ and six ___E:regional councils U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_council_(Israel))___ .

The ___E:Yesha Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yesha_Council)___ ( ___E:Hebrew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language)___ : מועצת יש"ע , Moatzat Yesha , a Hebrew acronym for ___E:Judea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judea)___ , ___E:Samaria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaria)___ and ___E:Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ ) is the umbrella organization of municipal councils in the West Bank.

The actual buildings of the Israeli settlements cover only one percent of the West Bank, but their jurisdiction and their regional councils extend to about 42 percent of the West Bank, according to the Israeli NGO ___E:B'Tselem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%27Tselem)___ .
Yesha Council chairman ___E:Dani Dayan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Dayan)___ disputes the figures and claims that the settlements only control 9.2 percent of the West Bank.
Between 2001 and 2007 more than 10,000 Israeli settlement units were built, while 91 permits were issued for Palestinian construction, and 1,663 Palestinian structures were demolished in Area C.
West Bank Palestinians have their cases tried in Israel's military courts while Jewish Israeli settlers living in the same occupied territory are tried in civil courts.
The arrangement has been described as "de facto segregation" by the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.

A bill to formally extend Israeli law to the Israeli settlements in the West Bank was rejected in 2012.  The basic military laws governing the West Bank are influenced by what is called the "pipelining" of Israeli legislation.

As a result of " ___E:enclave law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave_law)___ ", large portions of Israeli ___E:civil law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system))___ are applied to Israeli settlements and Israeli residents in the occupied territories.
On 31 August 2014, Israel announced it was appropriating 400 hectares of land in the West Bank to eventually house 1,000 Israel families.
The appropriation was described as the largest in more than 30 years.

According to reports on Israel Radio, the development is a response to the ___E:2014 kidnapping and murder of Israeli teenagers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_kidnapping_and_murder_of_Israeli_teenagers)___ .

In March 2024 and during the ___E:Gaza war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ , it was announced that Israel was planning on building more than 3,300 new homes in the ___E:Kedar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kedar_(Israeli_settlement))___ and ___E:Ma'ale Adumim settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%27ale_Adumim)___ in the West Bank. The consensus of the international community – the vast majority of states, the overwhelming majority of legal experts, the International Court of Justice and the UN – is that settlements are in violation of international law.   After the Six-Day War, in 1967, ___E:Theodor Meron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Meron)___ , legal counsel to the ___E:Israeli Foreign Ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Foreign_Ministry)___ stated in a legal opinion to the Prime Minister,

International intergovernmental organizations such as the Conference of the High Contracting Parties to the ___E:Fourth Geneva Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Geneva_Convention)___ ,  major organs of the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ ,  the ___E:European Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ , and ___E:Canada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)___ ,  also regard the settlements as a violation of international law. ___E:European Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ law requires a distinction to be made between goods originating in Israel and those from the occupied territories.

The Israeli Supreme Court has ruled that Israeli companies are entitled to exploit the West Bank's natural resources for economic gain, and that international law must be "adapted" to the "reality on the ground" of long-term occupation.

Due to the availability of jobs offering twice the prevailing salary of the West Bank (as of August 2013 [update] ), as well as high unemployment, tens of thousands of Palestinians work in Israeli settlements.

On 19 June 2011, Haaretz reported that the Israeli cabinet voted to revoke Defense Minister ___E:Ehud Barak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak)___ 's authority to veto new settlement construction in the West Bank, by transferring this authority from the Agriculture Ministry, headed by Barak ally ___E:Orit Noked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orit_Noked)___ , to the Prime Minister's office.

I will not be able to choke the settlements."  On 15 October 2009, he said the settlement row with the United States had been resolved.
In April 2012, four illegal outposts were retroactively legalized by the Israeli government.

In June 2012, the Netanyahu government announced a plan to build 851 homes in five settlements: 300 units in ___E:Beit El U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beit_El#Ulpana_lawsuits)___ and 551 units in other settlements.
Amid peace negotiations that showed little signs of progress, Israel issued on 3 November 2013, tenders for 1,700 new homes for Jewish settlers.
The plots were offered in nine settlements in areas Israel says it intends to keep in any peace deal with the Palestinians.

On 12 November, Peace Now revealed that the Construction and Housing Ministry had issued tenders for 24,000 more settler homes in the West Bank, including 4,000 in East Jerusalem.  2,500 units were planned in Ma'aleh Adumim, some 9,000 in the ___E:Gush Etzion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Etzion)___ Region, and circa 12,000 in the ___E:Binyamin Region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binyamin_Region)___ , including 1,200 homes in the ___E:E1 area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E1_(Jerusalem))___ in addition to 3,000 homes in previously frozen E1 projects.

Circa 15,000 homes of the 24,000 plan would be east of the ___E:West Bank Barrier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_West_Bank_barrier)___ and create the first new settlement blocs for two decades, and the first blocs ever outside the Barrier, far inside the West Bank.
As stated before, the Israeli government (as of 2015) has a program of residential subsidies in which Israeli settlers receive about double that given to Israelis in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem.
As well, settlers in isolated areas receive three times the Israeli national average.

From the beginning of 2009 to the end of 2013, the Israeli settlement population as a whole increased by a rate of over 4% per year. A New York Times article in 2015 stated that said building had been "at the heart of mounting European criticism of Israel."

___E:United Nations Security Council Resolution 2334 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_2334)___ "Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Council every three months on the implementation of the provisions of the present resolution;"   In the first of these reports, delivered verbally at a security council meeting on 24 March 2017, ___E:United Nations Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Special_Coordinator_for_the_Middle_East_Peace_Process)___ , ___E:Nickolay Mladenov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickolay_Mladenov)___ , noted that Resolution 2334 called on Israel to take steps to cease all settlement activity in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, that "no such steps have been taken during the reporting period" and that instead, there had been a marked increase in statements, announcements and decisions related to construction and expansion.

The 2017 ___E:Settlement Regularization in "Judea and Samaria" Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_Law)___ permits backdated legalization of outposts constructed on private Palestinian land. Following a petition challenging its legality, on June 9, 2020, Israel's Supreme Court struck down the law that had retroactively legalized about 4,000 settler homes built on privately owned Palestinian land.  The Israeli Attorney General has stated that existing laws already allow legalization of Israeli constructions on private Palestinian land in the West Bank.  The Israeli Attorney General, ___E:Avichai Mandelblit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avichai_Mandelblit)___ , has updated the High Court on his official approval of the use of a legal tactic permitting the de facto legalization of roughly 2,000 illegally built Israeli homes throughout the West Bank. [C] The legal mechanism is known as "market regulation" and relies on the notion that wildcat Israeli homes built on private Palestinian land were done so in good faith.

In a report of 22 July 2019, PeaceNow notes that after a gap of 6 years when there were no new outposts, establishment of new outposts recommenced in 2012, with 32 of the current 126 outposts set up to date. 2 outposts were subject to eviction, 15 were legalized and at least 35 are in process of legalization.
The Israeli government announced in 2019 that it has made monetary grants available for the construction of hotels in Area C of the West Bank.

According to ___E:Peace Now U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Now)___ , approvals for building in Israeli settlements in East Jerusalem expanded by 60% between 2017, when Donald Trump became US president, and 2019.

On 9 July 2021, Michael Lynk, U.N. special rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territory, addressing a session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, said "I conclude that the Israeli settlements do amount to a war crime," and "I submit to you that this finding compels the international community...to make it clear to Israel that its illegal occupation, and its defiance of international law and international opinion, can and will no longer be cost-free." Israel, which does not recognize Lynk's mandate, boycotted the session.
A new Israeli government, formed on 13 June 2021, declared a "status quo" in the settlements policy.

According to ___E:Peace Now U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Now)___ , as of 28 October this has not been the case. On October 24, 2021, tenders were published for 1,355 housing units plus another 83 in ___E:Givat HaMatos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Givat_HaMatos)___ and on 27 October 2021, approval was given for 3,000 housing units including in settlements deep inside the West Bank.  These developments were condemned by the U.S.  as well as by the United Kingdom, Russia and 12 European countries.   while UN experts, Michael Lynk, Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian Territory occupied since 1967 and Mr. Balakrishnan Rajagopal (United States of America), UN Special Rapporteur on adequate housing said that settlement expansion should be treated as a "presumptive war crime".

In February 2023, the ___E:new Israeli government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-seventh_government_of_Israel)___ under Benjamin Netanyahu approved the legalization of nine illegal settler outposts in the West Bank.  Finance Minister ___E:Bezalel Smotrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezalel_Smotrich)___ took charge of most of the ___E:Civil Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Civil_Administration)___ , obtaining broad authority over civilian issues in the West Bank.   In March 2023, Netanyahu's government repealed a 2005 law whereby four Israeli settlements, ___E:Homesh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homesh)___ , ___E:Sa-Nur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa-Nur)___ , ___E:Ganim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganim)___ and ___E:Kadim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadim)___ , were dismantled as part of the ___E:Israeli disengagement from Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_disengagement_from_Gaza)___ .

In June 2023, Israel shortened the procedure of approving settlement construction and gave Finance Minister Smotrich the authority to approve one of the stages, changing the system operating for the last 27 years.
In its first six months, construction of 13,000 housing units in settlements, almost triple the amount advanced in the whole of 2022.
